_about.purpose: Validate tier 3 (semantic). Every positive case is phrased so tiers 1 and 2 CANNOT fire: the skill is never named literally and no surface form is within fuzzy distance. Every negative case is chosen because it embeds close to a skill it does not represent.
_about.why_it_exists: The original 20-snippet set was saturated by tiers 1+2 (recall 1.000), so it could not measure tier 3 at all. A benchmark the baseline nearly solves is a benchmark with no signal left.
_about.labelling_protocol: Two annotators label independently, blind to model output. Disagreements are resolved by discussion and the pre-resolution labels are kept for Cohen's kappa. Do NOT label by running the model and agreeing with it.

_expected_behaviour.positives: Tiers 1+2 must score ~0.000 recall here by construction. Any recall above zero means a case is not actually paraphrase-only and should be moved to the main set.
_expected_behaviour.hard_negatives: Every match on a hard negative is a false positive. These drive the SEMANTIC_THRESHOLD choice — the knee is where negatives are suppressed without collapsing positive recall.
_expected_behaviour.success_criterion: There must exist a threshold where positive recall > 0.60 AND hard-negative false-positive rate < 0.10. If no such threshold exists, tier 3 is not carrying its weight and should be cut rather than shipped.
